name: Amazon Prime Air
description: Amazon's freighter scheme, worn by Amazon Air jets whichever contractor flies them: white forward fuselage with 'Prime Air' in big blue letters behind the cockpit; a Prime-blue band sweeps from the belly under the wing up to the crown ahead of the fin, and behind it the aft fuselage, tail cone and fin are a dark slate navy; the white Amazon smile (the curved arrow) low across the fin; white engines.

blue.name: Prime blue, as photographed (Amazon's brand Prime blue is #00A8E1)

navy.name: dark slate (reads navy in dull light; Amazon's 'squid ink' family)

areas.name: Prime-blue band from the belly under the wing up to the crown ahead of the fin
navy aft fuselage and tail cone behind the band

logos.description: The Amazon smile: a curved white swoosh, thin at its left end, thickest under the middle, rising to the right into an arrowhead whose point is at its upper right (the corner of a short hook that drops down and back). Low across the fin, about four-fifths of its chord wide. The right side shows the same logo unmirrored (arrowhead toward the nose there), per EI-AZC's right side (2026-03-18, see ATN/prime-air-blue).

titles.style: 'Prime Air' in big blue bold sans-serif, mixed case, italic (about 12°), behind the cockpit and forward door: Amazon's Prime wordmark lettering.

notes: Drawn on the 767-300 from N491AZ (2024-07-25), N643AZ (2026-05-12) and N337AZ (2021-11-09), all ATI-flown; every Amazon 767 photographed 2023-2026 wears it (N1327A, N1361A, N457AZ, N607AZ, N619AZ...). The 737-800 freighters wear a different, blue-bodied version: ATN/prime-air-blue. The Amazon A330-300P2Fs (Hawaiian/Alaska) aren't drawn: no open photo found. A small 'Operated by <contractor>' line under the cockpit windows changes with the operator (ATI, ABX, Atlas, Cargojet): left out; N643AZ adds a small 'Cloud Service' name there. No jet carries an 'Amazon Air' title although the airline was renamed Amazon Air in 2017: 'Prime Air' is the title on every painted jet seen. The slate runs over the crown just ahead of the fin; the belly under the blue band isn't seen in these photos and is assumed to wrap. Winglets: outer face white on N491AZ; a blue stripe shows on a winglet in the 2021 photo (not drawn). Horizontal tail gray. Amazon jets are tagged by registration in the airframes file of the airline whose callsign they fly under (ATN, ABX, GTI, CJT ...). Re-checked 2026-11-15 on the 767-300 (N491AZ 2024-07-25, N643AZ 2026-05-12): the title is italic, runs x 0.138-0.408 (length 0.27, both photos agree) with its cap top at y 0.56 (it had been drawn ~40% too tall); lowercase 0.72 of the capitals; the band's edges are curves (smooth). The band's upper edge ahead of x 0.7 reads 0.1-0.2 lower on the below-view photo than the above-view one: left as drawn.
history: New in Open Liveries (2026-11-13), not in Skyarium v1. The scheme came with Amazon's first leased 767s in 2016 ('Amazon One', N1511A, unveiled August 2016).
